:::{#sol-rank-factorization-practice}

[Columns of $\matr{A}$](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-column) are $(2, 1)$ and $(4, 2) = 2\,(2, 1)$,
so $\rankf{\matr{A}} = 1$, and

$$
\sbmat{2 \\ 1} \sbmat{1 & 2}
= \sbmat{2 \cd 1 & 2 \cd 2 \\ 1 \cd 1 & 1 \cd 2}
= \sbmat{2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2}
= \matr{A}.
$$

So $\matr{C} = \sbmat{2 \\ 1}$ ($2 \times 1$) and $\matr{R} = \sbmat{1 & 2}$ ($1 \times 2$)
are a rank factorization.

:::
